title: Quo (OpenPhone) Pricing in 2026: Starter, Business, Scale and Add-Ons
summary: Quo, formerly OpenPhone, lists Starter at $15, Business $23 and Scale $35 per user a month billed annually, or $19, $33 and $47 monthly. See what adds cost.
body_markdown:
Quo, the business phone app that used to be called OpenPhone, publishes prices for all three of its plans. Billed annually, Starter is $15, Business is $23 and Scale is $35 per user a month. Billed monthly, the same plans are $19, $33 and $47. Each user gets one phone number, and each additional number is $5 a month. There is a 7-day free trial. The pages were read on November 18, 2026.


Trellus publishes this guide and sells a dialer that some teams would choose instead. Every Quo detail below comes from Quo's own pricing page, rates page, fair use policy and help centre, opened on November 18, 2026. No price here comes from a review site. No Quo account was used and nothing was tested. Trellus also works inside Quo: see the[Trellus integration for Quo](https://www.trellus.ai/integrations/openphone) .


## Quo pricing at a glance


Quo's[pricing page](https://www.quo.com/pricing) has a switch between monthly and yearly billing. Quo is the current name of OpenPhone. The company's[about page](https://www.quo.com/about) describes it as Quo, formerly OpenPhone, and the old openphone.com pricing address now redirects to quo.com.


Quo plans per user a month in US dollars, from Quo's own pricing page and help centre, read on November 18, 2026. The page states no seat minimum. Plan Billed annually Billed monthly Seat minimum Free trial What is included for calling


Starter $15, billed as $180 a year $19 None stated 7 days One local or toll-free number per user, calling and messaging to US and Canadian numbers under a fair use policy, voicemail transcripts, manual call recording, the Quo API and the Sona AI agent. A shared number can have up to 10 paid users


Business $23, billed as $276 a year $33 None stated 7 days Starter plus call transfers, phone menus, group calling, custom ring orders, automatic call recording, AI call summaries and transcripts, analytics, and the HubSpot and Salesforce integrations


Scale $35, billed as $420 a year $47 None stated 7 days Business plus AI call tags, dedicated onboarding, priority support and inbound phone support


The pricing page lists no enterprise or custom plan. It says taxes and fees are added at checkout.


The trial terms come from Quo's[trial article](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/administration/billing/managing-your-trial) . The trial lasts 7 days and opens every feature, whichever plan was picked at signup. A credit card is required. Texting to US numbers and international calling are not available during the trial. Cancelling within the 7 days costs nothing.


## What changes the real cost of Quo


The seat price is public. The bill also depends on the billing cycle, extra numbers, texting registration, international usage and how much the AI agent is used.


### Annual or monthly billing


Annual billing lowers the monthly figure by $4 on Starter, $10 on Business and $12 on Scale. The page shows the saving as $48, $120 and $144 per user a year.


Quo's[subscription article](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/administration/billing/managing-your-subscription) says upgrades take effect at once with a prorated charge, and downgrades start at the next renewal. A user added in the middle of a cycle is billed a prorated amount straight away. A removed user's seat stays on the subscription until the end of the billing period and then drops off at renewal.


### Extra phone numbers


Each user includes one local or toll-free number. Additional numbers are $5 a month each on every plan. Quo's[plans and pricing article](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/administration/billing/pricing) says toll-free numbers cost the same as local ones, and that porting a number in is free, though third-party fees may apply.


### US carrier registration for texting


Texting US numbers requires registration with The Campaign Registry. The pricing page lists a one-time review fee of $19.50 and a monthly fee of $1.50 to $3. Quo's[carrier registration article](https://support.quo.com/getting-started/carrier-registration/carrier-registration) breaks the monthly fee down: $1.50 for most organisations, $2 for sole proprietors and $3 for non-profits. A rejected application costs $15 to resubmit.


### International calls and texts


Calls and texts to US and Canadian numbers are included. Other countries are billed per minute and per message from pre-paid credits. Quo's[rates page](https://www.quo.com/rates) lists a range for each country, because rates vary by carrier. On November 18, 2026, calls to Australia were listed at $0.05 to $0.33 a minute and texts at $0.11 each.


### Texts sent by automation


Texts sent from the Quo app to US and Canadian numbers are part of the subscription. Texts sent through the Quo API, Zapier or Make cost $0.01 per segment. Quo's[credits article](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/administration/billing/credits-and-usage) says these come out of the pre-paid balance, and that they fail if the balance runs out.


### Sona AI agent usage


Sona is Quo's AI agent that answers calls. It is included on every plan and billed in credits. One answered call uses 100 credits, and every workspace gets 1,000 credits a month, about 10 calls, at no charge. Quo's[Sona pricing article](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/ai-automations/sona/sona-pricing) says calls under 15 seconds do not count.


Sona automation credit tiers, from Quo's pricing page and Sona pricing article, read on November 18, 2026. One call uses 100 credits. Tier Price a month Credits included Calls covered Overage per call


Tier 1 $0 1,000 10 $1.00


Tier 2 $25 4,000 40 $0.75


Tier 3 $49 10,000 100 $0.65


Tier 4 $99 25,000 250 $0.55


Tier 5 $199 60,000 600 $0.45


Overages are off by default. When the credits run out, Sona stops answering and calls follow the fallback path in the call flow. If an admin turns overages on, extra calls are billed at the tier's rate.


### Taxes and fees


The plan prices exclude taxes and fees. The plans and pricing article says Quo collects federal, state and local telecommunication taxes and regulatory surcharges, such as 911 fees and the Federal Universal Service Fund. The amounts depend on the billing address and are not listed.


### Fair use limits


Calling and messaging to the US and Canada are marked unlimited with an asterisk. Quo's[fair use policy](https://www.quo.com/fair-use) says Quo may set limits or charge overages when usage is not normal business use. It states no number of minutes or messages.


### Cancellation


The pricing page's FAQ says a subscription can be cancelled in the app and stays active until the end of the billing cycle. The subscription article says payments already made are not refunded. The two pages differ on how long numbers are kept afterwards: the pricing page says 60 days and the help article says 30 days at most. Ask Quo which applies before cancelling.


## Who Quo fits and who it does not


Quo presents itself as a phone system for small businesses, startups and franchises. Its site says more than 90,000 businesses use it. That fits a team that wants one shared business line for calls and texts at a low public price.


It also fits a single user. The page states no seat minimum, so the smallest bill is one Starter seat at $19 on monthly billing, or $180 for a year.


Quo is a weaker fit for a team that needs call transfers, phone menus, automatic recording or the HubSpot and Salesforce integrations at the lowest price, because those start at Business.


It is also a weaker fit for high-volume outbound calling. The pricing page and plan comparison list no power dialer, parallel dialer or auto dialer on any plan. The fair use policy tells customers not to use auto-dialers or automated calling systems, not to call large numbers of unique or sequential numbers in a way that is inconsistent with normal business use, and not to place cold calls without proper consent. A team that plans to work through cold call lists should read that policy and confirm its use case with Quo first.


## Quo alternatives with published per-seat prices


These vendors print a seat price on their own pricing pages. Calling usage, numbers and taxes can be extra.


Published prices per seat a month. Aircall, Dialpad and JustCall figures come from this site's pricing guides, which read each vendor's pricing page on November 17, 2026. A dash means the page lists no such option. Product and plan Billed monthly Billed annually Lines Minimums and trial

**Trellus** is a Chrome extension that adds power and parallel dialing inside the CRM, sales engagement platform or spreadsheet a team already uses. It works with 31 platforms. The[Trellus power dialer](https://www.trellus.ai/power-dialer) plan, Power, is $99.99 per seat per month. The[Trellus parallel dialer](https://www.trellus.ai/parallel-dialer) plan, Power + Parallel, is $149.99 and calls up to five numbers at once. Both are bought online with no seat minimum. There is no free plan or free trial, and the Business plan is custom. The plan details are on[Trellus pricing](https://www.trellus.ai/pricing) .


Quo's list price is far lower than either Trellus plan and includes a phone number and texting. Trellus is a dialer for outbound lists, and texting is not listed in its plans.


Trellus also has a[Quo integration](https://www.trellus.ai/integrations/openphone) that calls an uploaded list one number at a time in the Quo web app. Quo's fair use policy restricts automated calling, so check with Quo before dialing lists on a Quo number.


For other public price lists, see[Dialpad pricing](https://www.trellus.ai/post/dialpad-pricing) ,[Aircall pricing](https://www.trellus.ai/post/aircall-pricing) and[JustCall pricing](https://www.trellus.ai/post/justcall-pricing) . See also the guide to[OpenPhone alternatives](https://www.trellus.ai/post/5-reliable-openphone-alternatives-for-streamlined-communication) .


## Frequently asked questions


### How much does Quo cost per user?


Quo's pricing page lists Starter at $15, Business at $23 and Scale at $35 per user a month on annual billing. On monthly billing they are $19, $33 and $47. Each user includes one phone number. Taxes and fees are added at checkout.


### Is Quo the same as OpenPhone?


Yes. Quo is the new name of OpenPhone. Quo's about page and help centre describe the product as Quo, formerly OpenPhone, and openphone.com now redirects to quo.com.


### Does Quo have a free trial?


Yes. Quo's help centre describes a 7-day trial with every feature unlocked. A credit card is required at signup. Texting to US numbers and international calling are not available until the account is on a paid plan.


### What costs extra on Quo?


Additional phone numbers are $5 a month each. US carrier registration for texting is $19.50 once, plus $1.50 to $3 a month. International calls and texts are billed per minute and per message. Automated texts sent through the API, Zapier or Make are $0.01 per segment. Sona calls beyond the 10 included each month are sold in credit tiers from $25 a month, or at $1.00 a call if overages are turned on.


### Does Quo include a power dialer?


No dialer is listed. Quo's pricing page and plan comparison show calling, texting, phone menus and call transfers, but no power, parallel or auto dialer. Its fair use policy also tells customers not to use auto-dialers or automated calling systems.
